transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well... I suppose I'm just having some trouble thinking clearly. My mind feels foggy. I work at a library, and lately I... I can't even keep my place in my old cataloguing notes. Or... decide what simple thing to do next. That's really why I'm here.
How long have you been noticing this trouble with concentration and mental fogginess—days, weeks, or longer?
It's been... a while. Probably about three months now. Most days are just... like this. It started around the time I began getting things ready to, um, to leave the library.
Over these past three months, have you noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

I suppose... yes. Most days lately, I just sit at the kitchen table and... it just feels like the color has gone out of everything. I don't know. Even my old watercolor books... looking at them just makes me feel heavy now, instead of interested. So... yes.
Over these past three months, have you also noticed feeling excessively worried or anxious about various things, more days than not?
No... I don't think so. I wouldn't call it worry. Just... what I mentioned before. I don't really feel anxious about things, just... tired of them, I suppose.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, or started any new medications or substances around the time this fogginess began?
No... nothing like that. I haven't been sick. No new medicines or... anything else. Just the same as always.
Do you notice this heaviness and foggy thinking even during times when you're not thinking about leaving the library, or does it mainly come up when that's on your mind?
I couldn't really say. I haven't... I haven't noticed if it's tied to that or not. It just seems to be there most of the time, I guess. I don't really keep track of it like that.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite, or a lack of energy, over these past three months?

Sleep is... well. I go to bed tired enough. But I always end up waking up around four in the morning. I just lie there... thinking about what I'm supposed to do with myself now. I don't really know about the rest of it. Just... tired, I guess.
Have you been having any thoughts of feeling worthless, excessively guilty, or thoughts that life isn't worth living?
I... no. Not really. I don't... I'm not thinking about dying or anything like that. Just... I don't know. I just feel like I said. Tired. I don't really dwell on... that other stuff.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight over these past three months?

I suppose... I don't really think about food much lately. I kind of have to remind myself to eat. My wife... she's the one who noticed, really. Says I leave my rice and soup half-finished. I never used to waste a meal before, so... yeah. Just not that hungry, I guess.

Do you notice this same sense of heaviness and lack of interest in other parts of your life that have nothing to do with the library—like time with your wife, or other hobbies—or does it seem to show up mainly when you're thinking about work?

It's... well, it's not just work. Most days lately, I just sit at the kitchen table. It feels like... I don't know, like the color has just gone out of everything. I used to like painting, watercolors... but now, even looking at my old watercolor books just makes me feel... heavy. I don't even want to pick up a brush. So... no, it's not just the library.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually elated, full of energy, needed much less sleep than usual, or were unusually impulsive or talkative?

I... well, I suppose there was a time. Right after I retired from my main job, before I took the library position. I had a few days where I just felt... I don't know, very bright. Almost too excited about things. I didn't need much rest. But... then I'd get irritable. My family would tell me to slow down, and I'd just get sharp with them over it. It was... just a phase, I think.
Thinking back to that time after your retirement, how many days in a row did that period of feeling unusually bright, energetic, and needing less sleep last?
I... I'm not really sure. I didn't count them. It was just... a few days, maybe? I wasn't keeping track of the calendar back then. Just a short while, I suppose.

During those few days after your retirement when you felt unusually bright and energetic, did the people around you notice a real change in how you were acting—like taking on many new projects, being unusually active, or doing things you normally wouldn't?

I suppose they noticed something. I... I did take on a bit more than usual. I started calling up old coworkers, trying to put together some sort of... lecture series. And I was planning out trips, setting up all these new watercolor projects. All at the same time. It was... well, it was a lot more than I'd usually do. I guess it was pretty obvious to them.

Over these past three months, has this fogginess and heaviness made it hard for you to manage your usual daily responsibilities—like taking care of yourself, household tasks, or activities you used to handle easily—or have you still been able to get through most of your day-to-day routine?

I... yeah, it's been hard. I haven't been keeping up. All those plans I made—the lecture series, the travel ideas—they're just sitting there. Piled up on the desk. Even just regular things, like the household paperwork... I can't seem to get through it. I just can't organize my thoughts the way I used to. It's... it's just been difficult.

Over the past three months, has this heaviness and fogginess gotten to the point where you're unable to go to work or interact with others at all, or have you still been able to manage some work and social contact, even if it's difficult?

I... well, like I said, I'm retired now, so there's no work to go to. But... I don't really see people much lately. The lecture plans, the travel notes... even just the regular household paperwork. It's all just piled up. I just... I can't organize myself the way I used to. So I mostly just stay home.
